newsitem.title: USA: May Brent shrinks in late U.S. paper trading.
newsitem.headline: May Brent shrinks in late U.S. paper trading.

text.p: North Sea Brent for May shrank in late U.S. paper trading on Wednesday, extending the day's weakness rooted in oversupply, traders said.
Four May Brent partials changed hands at $19.10, $19.14, $19.15 and $19.16 a barrel, down from $19.28 at the settlement of London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE).
Intermonth spreads were quiet in the aftermarket as they were over the course of the day, traders said.
April/May Brent was talked at -40/-38 cents a barrel. May/June was at -9/-6, while June/July was around -3/-1.
The May spread between West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent was at $1.38 a barrel.
